summary.text: A 58-year-old woman with metastatic hormone receptor-positive, HER2-low breast cancer, diagnosed in 2014 at age 48 with thoracic vertebral metastasis and treated with hormonal therapy, then paclitaxel with bevacizumab, then trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) in 2024, reported fatigue 17 days after the first T-DXd cycle.

The first episode showed elevated γGTP and CRP, positive blood cultures for Escherichia coli and CT intrahepatic bile duct dilation without definite obstruction. ERCP was not performed. Antibacterial treatment and conservative management led to symptomatic improvement and discharge on day 32.

On day 49 fever and jaundice recurred with elevated bilirubin, γGTP and CRP and CT bile duct stenosis and dilation. After antibiotic therapy, ERCP with biliary drainage tube insertion was done; biopsy showed fibrosis and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates without neoplasm and with scarce IgG4-positive cells. The authors state drug-induced cholangitis was diagnosed, but sclerosing cholangitis remained suspected.

Her performance status deteriorated and further chemotherapy was considered unfeasible. She opted for best supportive care, was discharged on day 71 and died on day 99; the source describes both death at home and death on day 99 of hospitalization.

caption_evidence.quote:
Fig. 1.
CT imaging. a CT imaging performed 17 days after the first cycle of T-DXd. Dilation of the intrahepatic bile ducts is observed, with no definite site of obstruction identified (arrow). b CT imaging performed 49 days after the first cycle of T-DXd. Mild dilation of the common bile duct wall is observed. A beaded appearance, characterized by alternating strictures and dilations with a periportal collar sign, is noted diffusely involving bile ducts in both hepatic lobes (arrows).

caption_evidence.quote:
Fig. 2.
Pathological findings. During ERCP, biopsies were obtained from four sites in the papilla, one site at the confluence of the right and left hepatic ducts, and one site from the distal bile duct. a Stromal fibrosis with infiltration of inflammatory cells, including neutrophils. No evidence of neoplastic lesions is detected. Obliterative phlebitis is not clearly identified. b IgG4+ cells are scarce. ERCP, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography.

caption_evidence.quote:
Fig. 3.
Trends in laboratory findings. At the time of the first administration of T-DXd, inflammatory markers and hepatobiliary enzymes were within normal ranges. On day 17, elevated CRP levels prompted antibiotic therapy initiation. Although CRP levels decreased, γGTP levels continued to rise. On day 49, when symptoms reappeared, elevations in CRP, γGTP, and TB were observed. Despite additional antibiotic administration and placement of an ERBD tube, CRP decreased, while γGTP and TB remained elevated. Hepatic transaminase levels remained within normal limits throughout treatment. Laboratory tests were not performed following the transition to home-based care. The patient died on day 99 of hospitalization. TB, total bilirubin; ERBD, endoscopic retrograde biliary drainage.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the 3 JPEGs were inspected in the separate visual submission.
Place of death is a source conflict: passed away at home versus died on day 99 of hospitalization (Fig. 3 caption); both sides review_only.

The diagnosis is suspected drug-induced sclerosing cholangitis; the day 49 paragraph says drug-induced cholangitis was diagnosed while the conclusion says a definitive diagnosis could not be established.
Values printed inside Fig. 3 (including AST/ALT and the γGTP point labelled 373 at Day 18) are pixel content only and are not compared with text values.
The agent causing the cholangitis cannot be attributed to a single drug among paclitaxel, bevacizumab and T-DXd (source limitation).
Introduction, discussion and literature-search statements about sclerosing cholangitis, other drugs and published cases are background, not patient facts.
